newsitem.title: USA: Diana faces suit for alleged insider trade.
newsitem.headline: Diana faces suit for alleged insider trade.

text.p: Attorneys for purchasers of Diana Corp's common stock during nearly a two-year period said Monday a class action has been filed accusing the company and some executives of insider trading.

The attorneys said the action accuses the defendants of artificially inflating and manipulating the trading price of the company's common stock by making false and misleading statements concerning product offerings, sales and revenues.
Diana could not immediately be reached for comment.

The attorneys said the suit also accuses the defendents of making well-timed transactions in the company's common stock designed to reflect interest in the stock and confidence in the company's products and accuracy of its public statements.
The attorneys said the class action was filed on behalf of purchasers of stock in the company between the period between December 6, 1994 and May 2, 1997.
The attorneys said the action was filed in the United States District Court for the Central District of California.
The suit names as defendends Diana, Sattel Communications LLC, Sattel Technologies Inc, Dawson-Samberg Capital Management Inc, Everest Capital Ltd and several individuals.
Plaintiffs seek to recover damages on behalf of all purchasers of Diana common stock during the class period.
Plaintiffs are represented by Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, law offices of Bernard Gross PC, Lowey Dannenberg Bemporad & Selinger PC and Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP.
